title: Assignment Super-Agent
description: Multi-agent CLI built on the Claude Agent SDK that classifies a university assignment brief and routes it through one of four pipelines — written work, data analysis, research, or coding — pausing for human approval after every stage. Each run ends with real deliverables plus an AI-assistance disclosure generated from what actually executed.

title: The AI Times — Personal AI Newspaper
description: Multi-agent system that collects AI news from ~25 curated sources (arXiv, lab blogs, global tech media, Hacker News), then runs a pipeline of Claude agents to filter, categorize, rank and summarize them into a daily broadsheet-style edition. FastAPI backend with a React reading UI; typical cost is a few cents per edition.

title: Job Application Agent
description: Local-first job-search agent for international students that ranks postings by H1B visa tier and AI fit score, tailors a resume per job, drafts cover letters and recruiter outreach, and tracks every application in Google Sheets with follow-up reminders. Human-in-the-loop by design — it only ever writes drafts, and never submits an application or sends a message.

title: Research Paper Agent
description: Runs the research-paper lifecycle end to end — CFP discovery, literature review, gap analysis, outlining, analysis, drafting — and verifies what it writes: every citation is re-resolved against publisher metadata, every claim fact-checked against its cited source, and every number traced to a real result. FastAPI and Next.js, exporting to LaTeX, DOCX and Markdown.

title: GVSU Admissions Chatbot
description: Answers prospective-student questions by searching gvsu.edu live rather than against a static index, reading the most relevant pages and returning a concise, grounded answer. Built out of admissions experience, where each question otherwise meant wading through unrelated search results. Claude for generation, Serper for search, containerized with Docker.

title: Tomato Disease Detection Service
description: Object-detection microservice that identifies disease on tomato leaves from a photograph. Packages a YOLOv5 model behind a containerized API with its own frontend, backed by a test suite and CI workflow.

title: Plant Leaf Health Classifier
description: Classifies plant leaf images as healthy or diseased and automatically rejects non-leaf photos. Logistic regression over EfficientNet-B0 features trained on PlantDoc (2,568 images, 38 disease classes), served by FastAPI behind a React frontend — with DVC for data versioning, MLflow for experiment tracking, Kubernetes for deployment, and GitHub Actions retraining and redeploying on every push.

title: Tomato Leaf Health Classifier
description: Binary classifier separating healthy tomato leaves from diseased or pest-infested ones, wired through a full MLOps pipeline: PlantDoc data versioned with DVC, experiments tracked in MLflow, the champion model served by FastAPI, containerized with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes.

title: Multi-Client Group Chat over TCP
description: Multi-threaded TCP group chat built from raw sockets for CIS 654, developed in three parts. The server acts purely as a relay — it spawns a thread per connection, tracks connected clients by username, and broadcasts each message to everyone except the sender, giving real-time chat with no message routing logic on the client side. Team project with Tyler Avink and Andrew DeVries.

title: RAG Chatbot for REP4FinLit
description: Retrieval-augmented chatbot backend for a LearnWorlds-hosted financial literacy platform, grounding answers in Azure AI Search over Azure OpenAI through a streaming FastAPI service. Hardened for a student-data setting: Presidio and spaCy strip PII for FERPA compliance, guardrails constrain responses, slowapi rate-limits callers, and managed identity replaces stored secrets. Every LLM call is traced as an OpenTelemetry span into Azure Monitor, with a retrieval evaluation suite covering the pipeline.

title: MLOps Toolchain Coursework
description: A record of my MLOps coursework at Grand Valley State University (Winter 2026), working through the production ML toolchain end to end — containerization, orchestration, experiment tracking, data versioning, and CI/CD for machine learning. The individual demo repositories are linked below.

title: Neural Networks: Classification vs Regression
description: Two PyTorch experiments contrasting how neural networks behave across task types: a multi-class classifier on the Iris dataset and a regression model on Boston Housing. Both are built from scratch as feedforward networks with two hidden layers, then compared through training curves and evaluation metrics under varying hyperparameters.

title: Merchant AI — Autonomous Trading Company
description: An AI-operated import/export business where software owns the full P&L loop — find, verify, buy, move, clear, stock, sell, collect, account — while a single human approves at eight defined gates. Built on an event-sourced trade state machine (19 states), a deterministic policy engine, and a balanced double-entry ledger, with every external touchpoint behind a mock/sandbox/live adapter. LLM judgment never bypasses policy code or a human gate.

title: FinBot — AI Budgeting Assistant
description: Interactive budgeting chatbot that walks users through setting financial goals and tracking income and expenses, returning AI-generated budgeting insights step by step. FastAPI backend against the OpenAI API with a React frontend.

title: FinBot — Student Budgeting Chatbot
description: An earlier, fully local iteration of FinBot aimed at students: LangChain over Ollama (Mistral) so no data leaves the machine, guiding users through student-specific income and expense categories via a chat interface and exporting the finished budget to Excel.

title: Fake News Detection
description: Binary classifier distinguishing real from fake news articles using TF-IDF features and a feedforward neural network, built for a Kaggle-hosted NLP challenge.

title: CNN Image Classification Challenge
description: Custom convolutional network (HighAccNet) trained end to end for an image-classification competition — image loading and preprocessing, training with best-checkpoint saving, and test-set inference written out in competition submission format.

title: Text-Based Wordle
description: Terminal implementation of Wordle with colored feedback output, built around loops, dictionaries, sets and file I/O — and covered by both unit tests for the engine functions and end-to-end tests for full gameplay.

title: Date Functions Library
description: Python module of date-handling functions built test-first: a complete set of black-box unit tests written against each function's specification before the implementations themselves, then used to verify them.

title: Electric Vehicle Population Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis of an electric vehicle population dataset — detecting and removing duplicate rows, resolving missing values, then visualizing the cleaned data to characterize the fleet.

title: Canadian Data Science Job Market 2024
description: Analysis of the Canadian data science job market using a LinkedIn dataset from early 2024 — job availability across provinces and cities, the distribution of roles and job types, the qualifications and experience levels employers seek, and sector-specific demand for data science skills.
